title: Long Xuyen Floating Market
text: Long Xuyen Floating Market takes place on the Hau River, starting near the O Moi ferry landing and stretching about 2 km along the bank. Traders sell fruit, vegetables and breakfast food directly from their boats. The market is busiest early in the morning, roughly 6 am to 8 am, and is quiet after 8 am. The market can only be reached by boat.

title: President Ton Duc Thang Memorial Site
text: The Memorial Site of President Ton Duc Thang is on Ong Ho Islet in My Hoa Hung, across the river from Long Xuyen. It stands where his childhood home was and was ranked a special national monument in 2012. The grounds include the old family house, a memorial temple and the Yak-40 aircraft that once carried him. Plan about 1.5 to 2 hours for a visit and dress neatly.

title: Ong Ho Islet and the ferry crossing
text: Ong Ho Islet sits in the middle of the Hau River, with a countryside of orchards, small canals and tree-lined paths that contrasts with the busy city. To get there, take the O Moi ferry or rent a private boat from the landing next to Long Xuyen Market. The island is named after a legend about a loyal tiger that guarded an old couple's graves.

title: An Giang Museum
text: An Giang Museum is on Thoai Ngoc Hau Street in My Long Ward and shows objects about the history and culture of the whole province. Visitors are advised to go in the morning or early afternoon so they have time to read the displays. Neat clothing is expected.

title: Ong Bac Pagoda
text: Ong Bac Pagoda is a Chinese-style temple at 68 Pham Hong Thai Street in My Long Ward. It reflects the Chinese heritage of the city, which mixes Kinh, Hoa and Khmer cultures. It is a quiet stop for architecture and photos.

title: Long Xuyen Cathedral
text: Long Xuyen Cathedral is at 9 Nguyen Hue A Street in My Long Ward. It is open to visitors every day of the week. Masses are held in the morning and in the evening.

title: My Phuoc Communal House
text: My Phuoc Communal House (dinh My Phuoc) is at 22 Ngo Thoi Nhiem Street. Visitors who want to see its festivals should come on the 11th and 12th days of the 12th lunar month, or on the 22nd and 23rd days of the first lunar month.

title: Long Xuyen Walking Street
text: The Long Xuyen walking street closes to vehicles from 6 pm to 11 pm on Fridays and Saturdays. During these hours it becomes a safe space for strolling, snacks and activities, with several attractions nearby.

title: Long Xuyen Crocodile Farm
text: The crocodile farm is along National Highway 91 and keeps thousands of crocodiles in large ponds inside a green compound. Visitors walk around and watch the animals from the pond edges.

title: Long Xuyen Night Market
text: Long Xuyen Night Market is a row of evening street food and snack stalls that locals visit after sunset. It is cheap and casual, and a good option for dinner or a light snack on a budget.

title: Bun ca Hieu Thuan
text: Bun ca Hieu Thuan serves Long Xuyen fish noodle soup at 18/2A Le Loi Street in My Binh Ward, opposite gate 2 of the Heart Hospital. It is open from 2 pm to 9 pm, and a bowl costs roughly 15,000 to 25,000 VND. The shop was run by a retired teacher couple and the dish was recognized as one of 50 famous specialties of Vietnam.

title: Bun ca Tu Lun by Nguyen Du Lake
text: Bun ca Tu Lun is a casual fish noodle shop near Nguyen Du Lake, at 20 Ly Thuong Kiet Street in My Binh Ward. It opens at 6 am and closes around 3 pm every day. A bowl costs about 20,000 VND, which makes it a cheap breakfast or lunch.

title: Com tam Cay Diep
text: Com tam Cay Diep is at 67 Ly Tu Trong Street in My Long Ward and serves Long Xuyen broken rice. A plate comes with grilled pork rib, shredded pork skin, pickles and braised egg, with the meat and egg cut into small pieces. Plates cost about 15,000 to 30,000 VND.

title: Lau mam Hieu Mienn
text: Lau mam Hieu Mienn serves fermented-fish hotpot, a classic Mekong Delta dish, at 5D Le Lai Street in My Binh Ward. It is open from 10 am to 8 pm. Prices range widely, from about 40,000 to 250,000 VND depending on the size of the pot.

title: Banh xeo 30/4
text: Banh xeo 30/4 is at 44 Le Quy Don Street in My Binh Ward and serves crispy Vietnamese savory pancakes filled with shrimp and pork, eaten with wild leaves and dipping sauce. Expect to pay about 20,000 to 50,000 VND per serving.

title: Best time to visit
text: The floating-water season, when fields flood and locals set traps and nets, runs roughly from the 8th or 9th to the 11th lunar month, depending on the source. For the floating market, go at sunrise, between about 5:30 and 8 am. One local operator says the week before Lunar New Year is an especially good time.

title: Getting to Long Xuyen
text: Long Xuyen is about 6 hours by road from Ho Chi Minh City, so a day trip from the south is not realistic and at least one night is recommended. There are frequent bus connections to Chau Doc and Can Tho. Chau Doc is about 50 km from Long Xuyen.

title: Where to stay and daily budget
text: Long Xuyen is an inexpensive city. Basic guesthouses cost around 200,000 VND per night, while mid-range hotels such as Hoa Binh 1 at 130 Tran Hung Dao Street are around 600,000 VND per room per night. Street food meals cost roughly 15,000 to 50,000 VND each.
